identity_evidence.quote: presented to our hospital with complaints of jaundice and abdominal distension

attribution_limitations: The first sentence calls the patient a man while the next sentence uses the pronoun She; both are kept as review-only and no sex is resolved.
The source says hepatobiliary enzymes were elevated without naming which analytes; no individual enzyme is flagged high.
Alectinib is described as low-dose although the dose was escalated to 600 mg; the discussion hedges that liver failure might have raised the blood concentration, which is not asserted as a cause.

Worsening anemia is said to occur "Concurrently" with rising T-Bil, but the source gives no calendar or day timing in the text; the time course exists only in the Figure 2 plot, whose values are not printed per point.

Parent decision: the liver biopsy is ordered after the improvement of liver failure because the sentence states it was performed once the liver failure had improved; the outcome event also bundles imaging over approximately 6 months, whose end is not ordered against the biopsy.
Presentation, CT, laboratory and EBUS-TBNA workup events carry no stated order relative to one another or to the diagnosis (diagnostic basis wording only); they are left unordered.

CT showed diffuse hepatomegaly and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Serum biochemistry showed elevated hepatobiliary enzymes, T-Bil 4.1 mg/dL and Child-Pugh Grade C, with markedly elevated CEA, NSE and CA19-9.

caption_claims.text: CT of the liver and mediastinum and histology and immunostaining of the mediastinal lymph node EBUS-TBNA specimen.

evidence.quote: Coronal section of the contrast‐enhanced chest and abdominal CT scan showing a significantly enlarged liver (a).

caption_claims.text: Course after starting alectinib: Hb, CEA and T-Bil plot, RBC transfusion arrows and a blood smear image.

evidence.quote:
FIGURE 2
The course after initiating alectinib treatment. The left vertical axis represents hemoglobin (Hb, g/dL) and CEA (ng/mL) levels, while the right vertical axis shows T‐Bil (mg/dL) levels. Red arrows indicate red blood cell (RBC) transfusions, with 2 units transfused per session. The peripheral blood smear image corresponds to the period of anemia, with red arrowheads indicating fragmented red blood cells. CEA, carcinoembryonic antigen.

caption_claims.text: Time course of liver CT after starting ALK inhibitors and liver needle biopsy histology and immunostaining.

evidence.quote:
FIGURE 3
Time course of transverse sections of the liver on contrast‐enhanced CT after initiating ALK inhibitors. (a) Transverse section of the liver on contrast‐enhanced CT at initial presentation. (b) Approximately 1 month after initiating alectinib. (c) At the time of lorlatinib initiation after discontinuing alectinib. (d) One month after starting lorlatinib. (e) Two months after starting lorlatinib. (f) Four months after starting lorlatinib. Pathological analysis of liver needle biopsy specimens with hematoxylin and eosin staining (g) and TTF‐1 staining (h), showing scattered cells with TTF‐1 positive atypical nuclei against a background of hepatocytes. Strong staining confirmed in tumor cells by ALK staining (i). ALK, anaplastic lymphoma kinase; CT, computed tomography.
